headline: West Virginia has an urgent educational problem that must be addressed
summary: Only 18% of West Virginia's 8th graders and 31% of 4th graders are proficient in math. State politicians have ignored recommendations from a Rand report to improve educational funding, including reforming the Hope Scholarship program which favors wealthier families over low-income ones. The state is considered among the least educated due to poor school quality and college attainment rates.

headline: In Oklahoma Trump country, locals say no to the president’s deal to build a foreign-owned smelter
summary: Hundreds of Inola residents protested against a proposed UAE-owned aluminum smelter due to environmental concerns. The project, backed by President Trump and Oklahoma's Republican Gov. Stitt, faces opposition from local leaders who have imposed a 60-day moratorium on permits. Residents demand written assurances about safety before supporting the project.

headline: Proposed NC budget would change funding for statewide remote charter schools
summary: The NC House passed a $34 billion state budget. A provision proposes changing how statewide remote charter schools receive funding, basing it on the statewide average instead of the district where their office is located, taking effect from 2027-28. This change aligns with the Department of Public Instruction's legislative priorities.

headline: Controversial NJ judge now overseeing immigration cases in Elizabeth
summary: A New Jersey judge appointed by the Trump administration to oversee immigration cases has sparked concern among attorneys due to his past comments and rulings deemed unsympathetic towards victims of domestic violence and sexual assault, potentially impacting migrant detainees seeking asylum or bond release.

headline: No prize yet for Blue Ribbon Commission. School funding formula retool is just getting started.
summary: Lawmakers delayed a decision on the Rhode Island Foundation's proposed overhaul of the state's K-12 education funding formula until 2027, forming a special commission to study its feasibility. The Blue Ribbon Commission's preferred model would increase the state's share from roughly 38% to 58%, costing an estimated $590 million annually. Some districts could see aid decreases, including regional district Chariho facing a potential $7.7 million reduction.

headline: Rhode Island is about to send millions of dollars to Washington. Here’s why.
summary: Rhode Island's leadership has passed legislation making it harder to opt into a federal scholarship tax credit program that could bring over $285 million in federal funds to support K-12 students locally. Gov. Dan McKee signed this legislation, and Democratic challenger Helena Foulkes vows to opt out altogether if elected. This decision is driven by teachers unions' opposition to the program, despite it not reducing public education funding or benefiting private schools most. The state's prioritization of union interests over students' needs is concerning, as student outcomes remain poor in cities like Providence.

headline: State budget extends Virginia higher education displacement commission funding for two years
summary: The Virginia state budget allocated over $300,000 for a commission studying Black communities' displacement by colleges and universities, marking its largest funding allocation to date. This is an increase from previous allocations of around $28,000 and $200,000 respectively. The additional funds will enable the commission to expand its scope of work and engage affected communities more actively over two years.

headline: Fabian Schmidt chose America long ago. A year after getting trapped in ICE’s net, he still does.
summary: Fabian Schmidt, a German green card holder living in Nashua, was detained by immigration officials at Boston Logan Airport for 16 hours due to a decade-old misdemeanor charge. He spent two months jailed in Rhode Island before being released following international attention and legal action. The incident reflects the Trump administration's aggressive immigration crackdown, impacting lawful immigrants like Schmidt who were not previously targeted.

headline: McMorrow suspends U.S. Senate campaign
summary: Michigan's Democratic U.S. Senate primary now a two-way race between Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed after Mallory McMorrow suspends campaign; winner to face Republican Mike Rogers in November. No significant protests or civil unrest reported related to this political development.
